figureAudit.note: decksTotal counts transcribed decks; 'available' counts the 2026 edition's nine decks only. All five decks were transcribed by Sonnet from their native 1280x720 page JPEGs and audited by a separate Sonnet agent with enlarged crops. Lecture 1: 14 table-, chart-, number- and code-heavy pages, 0 discrepancies; the parent also checked slides 39 and 106 and a crop of slide 86. Lecture 2: 18 diagram-, equation-, code- and heat-map pages (7, 8, 24, 26, 27, 28, 36, 44, 53, 54, 56, 63, 72, 75-77, 79, 80), 2 small discrepancies fixed (a code-indentation note on slide 28, an ellipsis that is not on slide 63); the parent also checked slides 77 and 79. Lecture 3: 19 matrix-, kernel-, formula-, code-, chart- and diagram-heavy pages (12, 13, 16, 27, 29, 30, 36, 40, 41, 46, 47, 49, 53, 54, 57, 61, 63, 65, 68), discrepancies on 6 of them, all fixed: slide 12's stated digit uncertainty was unfounded (all 192 cells matched); slide 29's X is 9x9, not 8x8; the green boxes on slides 53-54 and slide 53's mixed quote marks; slide 57 has five reader points per panel, not four, and only panel b labels its y-axis; slide 61's dots. The parent also checked slides 57 and 65 and found slide 65's loss printed with one closing parenthesis, which reader and auditor had both balanced. Lecture 4: 22 equation-, chart-, diagram- and photograph-heavy pages (5, 7, 17, 23, 28, 29, 31, 35-37, 41, 55-57, 62, 70, 72, 74, 76, 79, 80, 84), discrepancies on 6, all fixed: the scatter plots' tick labels on slides 28-29 were readable after all (-4 to 4), and slide 29's colour bar has twelve colours, not ten; slide 62's point order; slide 74's N is upright; slide 76's noise points and strip backgrounds; slide 80's play button and logo. Nothing described was absent from its page. The parent also checked slides 70 and 29 (the GAN objective and the KL expansion, both exactly as printed) and a crop of slide 77. Lecture 5: 22 chart-, table-, equation- and diagram-heavy pages (7, 15, 17-19, 22, 26, 28, 30-33, 37-40, 42, 46, 48, 52, 53, 56), discrepancies on 6, all fixed: slide 32's second convolution block; slide 33's three tildes were error-bar caps, the grey bar exceeds the blue on four games rather than one, and the legend's form; the position of the braces on slides 37 and 40; slide 38's axis arrowheads and bar ratio; slide 48's frame list. Nothing described was absent from its page; slide 33's 49 labels and slide 52's table were exact. The parent also checked slides 33 and 46 (the policy-gradient loss and update, exactly as transcribed) and a crop of slide 33's labels.

images.note: Lecture 1: 34 of 108 pages; lecture 2: 33 of 83 pages; lecture 3: 33 of 70 pages; lecture 4: 39 of 84 pages; lecture 5: 19 of 58 pages; in each, every slide with a distinct figure. caveats: Covers lectures 1-5 of the 2026 edition only: 5 of the catalog's 90 recordings.

The decks are flattened PDFs with no text layer and no printed slide numbers. Slide N is PDF page N, and everything in raw/slides/ was read visually from 1280x720 page images; there is no higher-resolution source.
Transcripts are YouTube auto-captions, lightly copy-edited. The verbatim captions are in raw/transcripts/original/.
Slide images are 1280x720, the deck's native resolution, below the 1400px used in sibling KBs.

Some slide code and formulas are reproduced as printed, including the slides' own slips (lecture 1: slide 82's tf.keras.optimizer, slide 86's update step; lecture 2: slide 27 writes matrix products with *, slide 28's 'from tf.keras.layers import SimpleRNN'; lecture 3: slides 53-54 pass filter_size where slide 47 uses kernel_size, slide 54 calls nn.Sequential with only torch imported, slide 65's loss has an unclosed parenthesis; lecture 4: slide 29's KL-divergence expansion carries a leading minus sign that makes it never positive, slide 41 overprints two labels and leaves an empty box where beta would go; lecture 5: slide 42 labels its third point (s_2, a_3, r_2)); the slide files note each one.
Lecture 2's slides and lecturer call the scaled dot product of query and key the 'cosine similarity', and give its denominator only as 'scaling'; the wiki reports this as the course states it.
Lecture 2 says vision transformers will be covered in lecture 3; lecture 3 as delivered covers convolutional networks and does not mention them.

Lecture 4's GAN objective (slides 70-72) is printed as log D(G(z)) + log(1 - D(x)) with the first term labelled 'Fake'; the lecturer reads it so that D is the probability of fake, while the deck's number-line slides plot the probability of real. The wiki reproduces the formula as printed and states both readings.
Lecture 4's slides 40-41 (disentanglement, beta-VAEs) are not discussed in the talk; the wiki covers them from the slides alone.

Lecture 5's Q-loss (slide 30) is printed as the expectation of a squared norm, and described aloud as an absolute value; asked whether the target, which contains Q(s', a'), depends on the network, the lecturer calls it 'the actual reward' and the notation 'probably a misnomer'. The wiki reports both as the course states them.
Lecture 5 showed, in answer to a question, a slide on training game-playing agents from scratch that is not in the published deck; the wiki describes it from the talk alone.
